title: fix(react): an authored objectFields never reaches a component prop (objectui#8818)
body:
Fixes #8818
Clause-②: no

This PR carries out the ratified class-one ruling on objectui#8818 (comment `5653291246`, letter a, ratified in `5810248981`). `objectFields` joins `SchemaRenderer`'s fixed metadata strip list, so an authored value can no longer reach a component prop. That completes decision batch #70 (objectui#7742 / PR objectui#8799), which ruled that `objectFields` is a React prop and not a schema key.

Author: `domain:ui` seat 1, a dispatched dev run under claim `5830962988`, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`.

## Premise, re-measured on `origin/main` `f5178a272`

- `objectFields` in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`: 0 hits (grep exit 1). The control, `className`, has 22 hits on the same query.
- The bug reproduced before the fix. A test-registered probe, rendered through the real `SchemaRenderer`, received an authored `objectFields` as a prop in all three authoring spellings: top-level, `properties`, and the legacy `props`. On the base tree, the rows that assert the key never arrives failed and the control rows passed (5 failed, 11 passed).

## Step 1: the census of every non-test reader

Instrument: `git grep -n -w objectFields` over `packages/*/src/**`, tests excluded. It finds 128 lines in 22 files; the control, `className`, hits 702 files on the same pathspec. Outside `packages/*/src` the key appears only in `.changeset/` prose. No JSON document, example, doc page or app authors it. There are 9 member reads (`.objectFields` or `['objectFields']`), and all 9 read `WidgetContext` in metadata-admin.

Classes: (i) a React prop that a host passes through JSX or `createElement`; (ii) a node key that arrives through `SchemaRenderer`'s spread; (iii) a local variable, function parameter or context field that is not a component prop.

| site (file · symbol) | how the value arrives | class | changed by the strip? |
|---|---|---|---|
| plugin-kanban `index.tsx` · `KanbanRenderer` / `KanbanRendererProps.objectFields` | JSX prop from `ObjectKanban` (`objectFields={objectDef?.fields}`). No registry key resolves to `KanbanRenderer`; the only registration is `object-kanban`, which maps to `ObjectKanbanRenderer`. | i | no |
| plugin-kanban `KanbanImpl.tsx` · `KanbanBoard`, `KanbanBoardInner`, `SortableCard`, `getCardStyles` | JSX props forwarded from `KanbanRenderer` | i | no |
| plugin-kanban `ObjectKanban.tsx` · `ObjectKanban` | the producer: passes `objectDef?.fields` as a prop and discards its own rest-spread (`void _props;`) | i | no |
| plugin-kanban `requiredWhenPrompt.ts` | function parameter, called with `objectDef.fields` | iii | no |
| plugin-grid `ObjectGrid.tsx` · 4 JSX sites | the producer: `objectFields={objectSchema?.fields}` into `RowActionMenu`, `BulkActionDialog` and `BulkActionBar` (twice) | i | no |
| plugin-grid `RowActionMenu.tsx`, `BulkActionBar.tsx`, `BulkActionDialog.tsx` | JSX props from `ObjectGrid`; none of these is a registered component | i | no |
| plugin-grid `useBulkExecutor.ts` | hook option passed by `BulkActionDialog` | iii | no |
| plugin-detail `DetailView.tsx` | local `const objectFields = objectSchema?.fields` | iii | no |
| app-shell metadata-admin `widgets.tsx`, `SchemaForm.tsx`, `ResourceEditPage.tsx`, `ViewVariantInspector.tsx` · `WidgetContext.objectFields` | a context object passed as the `widgetContext` JSX prop; none of these files imports `SchemaRenderer` | iii | no |
| app-shell `ViewColumnInspector.tsx`, `FlowReferenceField.tsx`, `ViewConfigPanel.tsx`, `IdentityImportPanels.tsx` | local variables and function parameters | iii | no |
| plugin-kanban `KanbanRecordsSettled.ts`, plugin-grid `multiValueFields.ts`, types `objectql.ts`, `zod/objectql.zod.ts` | comments only | none | no |

⇒ **There is no class (ii) reader.** No host writes the catalogue into a schema node it renders, and no `SchemaRenderer` call site passes `objectFields` in any form. So the fork the claim warns about does not exist. Every census site keeps working by construction, because none of their values passes through the stripped channel.

## Step 2: the strip, including the second prop-building site

`SchemaRenderer` builds a component's props from two authored bags. This PR closes both, in the one claimed file:

1. **The metadata destructure that feeds `...componentProps`.** `objectFields` is added next to `testId`, with a comment that cites batch #70. This covers a top-level `objectFields` and `properties: { objectFields }`, because the evaluation memo hoists `properties.*` onto the node before the destructure runs.
2. **The legacy `props` alias bag.** It is spread as its own bag after the destructure, so the destructure never sees it; objectui#9758 found the same carrier for `data`. A new helper, `withoutAuthoredObjectFields`, removes the key on every arm. It runs **before** the objectui#9758 `data` strip, because that strip's diagnostic decides by object identity.

Other paths were checked, and none passes the key on as a prop:
- `ariaProps` and `debugAttrs` are computed from named keys.
- The `data-*` attributes are a fixed set: `data-obj-id`, `data-obj-type`, `data-testid` and `data-obj-schema-invalid`.
- `SchemaErrorBoundary` and the lazy-loading placeholder receive no node spread.
- The host's own `...props` is spread last. That is the ruled channel, and it still delivers.

No published type or export changes.

## Pins: `packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.objectFieldsStrip-8818.test.tsx` (16 tests)

- Row 1, for three type keys (a plain probe, `object-grid` and `object-kanban`): all three authoring spellings lose the prop seat.
- Row 2 (control): a sibling key authored the same three ways still arrives, which shows the probe is live.
- Rows 3–4 (host control): an `objectFields` passed by the host still arrives, and it wins over an authored value in every spelling.
- Row 5: `objectFields` is the only key removed from the alias bag.
- Row 6: on the object arm, stripping the alias key is not misreported as a refused `data`.
- Row 7: the objectui#6708 dropped-bag notice no longer names `objectFields`, but it still names the other keys.
- Row 8: a node that authors no `objectFields` gets exactly the same key set as before.

## Ablation: on disk, via `ablation-replace.mjs`, on head `4f3a1878f`

The anchor must hit before anything is written, and each restore is proven by blob hash.

| leg | mutation | red | green | restore |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | delete the destructure entry `objectFields: _objectFields,` | row 1 (all three type keys): the top-level and canonical spellings arrive again; the legacy spelling stays absent | 13, including host rows 3–4 | blob equals HEAD `364d47f781de`; `git diff HEAD` empty |
| B | make the `withoutAuthoredObjectFields` guard always return the bag unchanged | row 1 (all three type keys, legacy spelling arrives), rows 5 and 7 | 11, including host rows 3–4 | same |
| C | move the alias strip after the `data` strip | row 6 only | 15 | same, for both nested legs |

The pin imports `../SchemaRenderer` by a relative path, so it reads `src/` directly and no build sits between a mutation and the run.

## Gates at the code head `284308295` (the prose-only round `8b331df77` re-ran its own gates; they are recorded in the seat's ACCEPT on objectui#8818)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/` from the repo root: 98 of 98 files passed, 1323 of 1323 tests. That file count equals the number of tracked test files under `packages/react`.
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/react^...' build`, then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react type-check`: exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes the new pin.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: OK. `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: 1 changeset declared for 1 released package.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: the self-contradiction reading passes. The gate lists 4 pending changesets that name `SchemaRenderer.tsx`: `5926-empty-action-visible-when`, `7319-dead-schemarenderer-retired`, `7415-action-type-input-rename` and `9959-refused-data-prop-warn-reset`. Each paragraph was read, and all four are still true; none of them is about the strip list.
- Also run: `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:unreferenced-sources` and `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, all exit 0. The `plugin-kanban` pins `objectFieldsIsAPropNotASchemaKey-7742` and `kanban-family-registry-keys-retired-8257` pass 12 of 12, and neither is edited.
- eslint over the touched files, per-rule counts against base: `SchemaRenderer.tsx` is unchanged (18 `no-explicit-any` and 1 `exhaustive-deps` warnings, 0 errors). The new test has 0 errors and 0 warnings. The eslint config has no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the three paths: NOT GOVERNED.

## Acceptance notes

1. **Prose that this change made false, corrected in this PR** (seat ruling B on the dev's open question; head `8b331df77`, prose only, no code token or assertion changed). The seat extended the claim's surface for exactly these seven sites, after measuring that none of them overlaps PR objectui#10588's hunks (`index.tsx` 452–471, the 8802 changeset 138–147):
   - `packages/plugin-kanban/src/index.tsx`, the `KanbanRendererProps.objectFields` JSDoc (ships in `.d.ts`): it now says the key is closed at `SchemaRenderer`'s boundary since objectui#8818. The stale "`kanban-ui` registration below" and "`ObjectKanbanRenderer` serves `type: 'kanban'`" sentences were corrected in the same block.
   - The same file, the `kanban-ui` retirement docblock: "This closes the ENTRY, not the CLASS …" now records that the class is closed as well.
   - `packages/plugin-kanban/src/__tests__/kanban-family-registry-keys-retired-8257.test.ts`: the file header and the suite-3 prose are corrected, and the suite-3 `describe` and the test titled "the CLASS is still open" are renamed to what their unchanged assertion (`objectFields?: unknown;` is still declared) proves.
   - The pending changesets `8802-8257-8008-kanban-gantt-family-retirement` and `7742-kanban-arm-batch70` each gain an insert-only "Superseded in this release by objectui#8818: …" paragraph. Frontmatter is byte-identical and zero lines are deleted. This PR's own changeset no longer carries a supersedes paragraph.
2. **What the strip does not do.** This is how the strip list already works, and it is unchanged. The node still reaches the component as `schema`, and the raw `properties` and `props` bags still reach it as values. So an authored catalogue can still be read at `schema.objectFields` or inside those bags. The census found zero such readers, and ruling item 1 already classes any future reader as a bug of this same class.
3. **Registry dispatch outside `SchemaRenderer`.** `action-bar`, the form field widgets, `MarkdownImpl` and the report renderers call `ComponentRegistry.get` themselves. None of them resolves to a component that reads `objectFields`, so nothing leaks today. Recorded here, not carded.
4. **Where the pin lives.** Ruling item 2 names PR objectui#8799's pin file as the place for the new negative leg. The claim's file surface and the card constraint put the pins next to the `SchemaRenderer` strip tests instead. The `kanban-ui` registration that leg would have exercised is also retired. The existing 7742 pin still covers the prop path for `KanbanRenderer` and is untouched.
5. **Docs.** No docs page or README lists the strip list or mentions `objectFields`. The changeset states the host channel.
